newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African minister backs hunting.
newsitem.headline: South African minister backs hunting.

text.p: A South African minister said on Tuesday that allowing tourists to hunt wild animals was a better way of helping to feed the country than using the land to grow food.

Land and Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom made the remarks to a parliamentary agriculture committee in response to a member of parliament who said much land in South Africa was wasted on animals when humans were crammed into areas that did not give them room to grow food.

"All indications are that in certain areas combinations of domestic animals that graze and (wild) animals that browse constitute better utilisation of land, and you'll get a better protein off-take from that land," Hanekom said.

"On the other hand, if...you've got an American tourist who's prepared to pay $30,000 for a bit of trophy hunting, and that money goes into the community, you'll get a lot more food out of that money than you would ever have got out of just growing food," he said.
